dct_description_sm: This layer is a georeferenced raster image of the historic paper map entitled: Plan von Dresden : 1902, Bearbeitet vom Vermessungsamte der Stadt Dresden. It was published by Giesecke & Devrient in 1902. 16th Aufl. Scale 1:10,000. Covers the Dresden region, Germany. Map in German. The image inside the map neatline is georeferenced to the surface of the earth and fit to the Deutsches Hauptdreiecksnetz (DHDN) 3-degree Gauss-Kruger Zone 5 coordinate system. All map collar and inset information is also available as part of the raster image, including any inset maps, profiles, statistical tables, directories, text, illustrations, index maps, legends, or other information associated with the principal map. This map shows features such as roads, railroads and stations, drainage, built-up areas and selected buildings, city districts, parks, ground cover, and more. Includes inset: Erganzungsblatt zu der Flur Reick. This layer is part of a selection of digitally scanned and georeferenced historic maps from The Harvard Map Collection as part of the Imaging the Urban Environment project. Maps selected for this project represent major urban areas and cities of the world, at various time periods. These maps typically portray both natural and manmade features at a large scale. The selection represents a range of regions, originators, ground condition dates, scales, and purposes.
